title: US equity, options and bond markets closed — New Year's Day (Friday 2027-01-01, the holiday that makes 2026-12-31 the year's last session)
source: NEWS: nyse.com/markets/hours-calendars, fetched direct 2026-09-08 (HTTP 200 after its 302, 109,180 bytes) and parsed cell by cell by the christmas-market-closure-2026-12-25 initial research. The New Year's Day row parses as ['Thursday, January 1', 'Friday, January 1', '—*'] for 2026 / 2027 / 2028, so 2027 is a full closure on Friday January 1; the em dash in the 2028 cell carries footnote *, which reads verbatim 'Because the holiday falls on Saturday, January 1, 2028, no New Year's Day holiday is observed' — the contrast that proves the 2027 cell is a real observed closure and not a formatting artifact. CORROBORATED FROM TWO FURTHER PRIMARIES THE SAME SESSION. (1) SIFMA's US Holiday Recommendations 2026 panel (sifma.org/resources/guides-playbooks/holiday-schedule, HTTP 200, 299,272 bytes) carries a 'New Year's Day 2026/2027' row giving a full US fixed-income close on 'Friday, January 1, 2027' with 'Early Close (2:00 p.m. Eastern Time): Thursday, December 31, 2026'. (2) The OCC's own expiration calendar (www.optionseducation.org/api/expirationcalendar, HTTP 200, 34,871 bytes) marks 2027-01-01 {"holiday":{"description":"Exchange/OCC holiday","hatched":true}} — and the same file's vocabulary is what makes that marker load-bearing rather than decorative: it reserves 'Exchange/OCC holiday' (hatched) for full closures and uses a separate 'Bank holiday' label for the bond-only days when equities stay open (2026-10-12 Columbus Day, 2026-11-11 Veterans Day). Reproduced by statute and weekday arithmetic: 5 U.S.C. 6103 fixes New Year's Day on January 1, and January 1 2027 is a Friday, so it is observed on the day with no shift. Filed estimate on the two standing counts: the confirmed-prefix taxonomy in market-events-data.ts has no slot for an exchange's or a trade association's own holiday calendar, and a discovering lane may not self-confirm an event it found in-sweep. Checked 2026-09-08
notes: PROPOSED by the christmas-market-closure-2026-12-25 initial research (2026-09-08), found inside its own corridor: this closure is 7 days after the proposer's event and is what makes Thursday 2026-12-31 the LAST SESSION OF 2026 rather than the second-to-last. That fact is load-bearing for the proposer's ledger and for at least four entries this calendar already dates to 2026-12-31 (sp-select-sector-secondary-reweight-2026-12-31, russell-style-quarter-end-capping-effective-2026-12-31, sifma-bond-early-close-2026-12-31, jpx-market-closure-2026-12-31), none of which can state what follows their own date without it. THE 2026-12-31 SESSION IS THE DENSEST ESTIMATE CLUSTER IN THE CORRIDOR and it is unusually loaded for a year-end: seven tracked entries, a FULL NYSE equity session, an OCC quarterly expiration (www.optionseducation.org/api/expirationcalendar marks it 'Quarterly Expiration date', legend GUID 812CD242-1E6F-48D4-A1CB-9608ABD8344F), and a SIFMA-recommended 2:00 p.m. ET US bond early close — with this closure directly behind it. THE CONTRAST WORTH CARRYING FORWARD: christmas-market-closure-2027-12-24's ledger records that the 2027 year-end early close sits in front of NO holiday at all, because Saturday New Year 2028 is not observed (NYSE footnote *). 2026 is the inverse — its year-end early close sits in front of a real observed Friday holiday. Two consecutive year-ends with opposite structure is exactly the kind of thing a lane re-derives wrong from a template, which is the argument for the row. Low impact: a scheduled closure known 115 days ahead moves no price and licenses nothing. Kind sector, symbols empty and status estimate reuse the settled precedent every US trading-hours entry in this calendar follows. Note the id names the holiday rather than the observance date because there is no shift in 2027; a sibling lane reaching 2028 should expect no equivalent entry, per footnote *.
